title: Motives to receive the word are only moral arguments
source_text: XXVII. Cum autem, ut ante dictum est, hanc esse divinam revelationem, & illud esse Dei verbum, res non sit mathematice, seu logice demonstrabilis, incitamenta & media illa, quae nos movent ad Dei verbum ut tale suscipiendum, non possunt esse plusquam argumenta moralia, quae non mathematice, sed moraliter evidens faciunt menti bene affectae quod proponitur tanquam Dei verbum, & doctrina coelestis, revera in se tale esse. Adeoque argumenta illa non possunt ex se menti ingenerare, nisi certitudinem illam, quam moralem diximus, & quae ex suo genere inferior est illa certitudine, qua principiis per se notis, & conclusionibus inde evidenter deductis assentimur. Etenim, licet homo cujus mens intus Dei Spiritu illustrata, & qui ad notas & varia τεκμήρια verbi Dei debite attendit, judicet & videat impossibile esse ut ab alio quam a Deo prodierit, probationes tamen inde deductae, quibus impellitur ad ita judicandum, non nisi morales sunt, & quod istud videre dicitur non de alia quam de morali evidentia intelligi debet.
pass_a_gloss: But since, as was said before, that this is divine revelation and that that is God’s word is not a matter mathematically or logically demonstrable, those incentives and means which move us to receive God’s word as such cannot be more than moral arguments, which make not mathematically but morally evident to a well-affected mind that what is proposed as God’s word and heavenly doctrine is truly such in itself. And so those arguments cannot of themselves generate in the mind anything but that certainty which we have called moral, and which in its own kind is inferior to that certainty by which we assent to principles known through themselves and to conclusions evidently deduced from them. For although a man whose mind is inwardly illuminated by God’s Spirit, and who duly attends to the marks and various tokens of God’s word, may judge and see that it is impossible it came from another than God, yet the proofs thence deduced by which he is driven so to judge are only moral, and that ‘seeing’ must be understood of no other than moral evidence.
pass_b_english: Motives ≤ moral arguments → only moral certainty of themselves.
Spirit-illumined ‘seeing’ still = moral evidence, not scientia-grade.

choices.term: non possunt esse plusquam argumenta moralia

rejected: motives yield mathematical demonstration that the word is God’s
